cohort: Every TypeScript trial at portfolio rank 1 from round 8: N09, N10, P7.
hypothesis: Paired compiler diagnostics can expose newly introduced argument/receiver type conflicts that a runtime transpiler and semantic reviewer miss.
configuration: Nearest source tsconfig and exact installed TypeScript version inside each recorded image; no network.
comparison: Compile the control snapshot and generated snapshot; compare diagnostic multisets inside exact generated-test AST regions.
limitations: Candidate type declarations can be wrong. Diagnostics are counterevidence, not final oracle truth.
Do not reject issue-promised behavior solely because a candidate type declaration omits it.
No generalization or detector claim from this three-trial diagnostic probe.

adapter_failures: First N10 attempt used the runtime-qualified test ID rather than the source registration name.
Second N10 attempt compiled successfully but wrote the detailed report outside the persistent logs directory. Summary reported one new diagnostic.
Both attempts remain recorded; final three runs retained full reports.
conclusion: Each first-rank TypeScript program introduces a concrete type conflict. This exposes useful information absent from runtime transpilation and compact semantic review. Validate known-positive TypeScript programs before using any rejection policy; type declarations may themselves be incomplete or buggy.
